{{city-state|Brooklyn|New York}} | former_school(s)= | career_highlights = | awards = | honors = | records = | championships = | championship_list = | tournaments = | tournament_list = }} '''Lance Stephenson, Jr.''' (born September 5, 1990 in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City]]) is an [[United States of America|American]] college [[basketball]] player. He is a {{height|ft=6|in=5}} [[shooting guard]] and attended [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn, New York)|Lincoln High School]] in the [[Coney Island]] section of Brooklyn.Corcoran, Tully. [http://www.cjonline.com/stories/102607/haw_212251538.shtml "KU attracts Brooklyn star"], ''[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]]'', October 26, 2007. Accessed September 17, 2009. "Lincoln High School in [[Brooklyn]], N.Y., is to high school basketball what [[Odessa, Texas|Odessa]] [[Permian High School]], in Texas, is to high school football. Basketball rules there. Stephon Marbury starred there. Marv Albert went there. Even Jesus Shuttlesworth, the fictional baller played by Ray Allen in ''[[He Got Game|He'ssic Got Game]]'' went there. Kansas coach Bill Self may be spending a bit of time there in the next year, too. Lance Stephenson, a 6-5, 195-pound junior guard from Lincoln who is the No. 4 overall player in the class of 2009 recently contacted Self about his interest in Kansas." Stephenson won city basketball championships in all four years of high school, is [[New York State]]'s all-time leading scorer in high school basketball. After his Senior year he was named [[New York Mr. Basketball Award|New York State Mr. Basketball]] and was named to the [[McDonald's All-American Team]] in 2009. ==High school career== Stephenson first caught the attention of scouts at age 12, when Clark Francis, a talent evaluator, saw him play at Rumble in the Bronx [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] tournament. And before his first year of high school, he attended the Adidas ABCD Camp, where he challenged [[O.J. Mayo]] to a one-on-one game.{{cite news |title=What's next for Lance Stephenson? The world will find out soon |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/the_bonus/03/27/lance.stephenson/index.html |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |first=Kevin |last=Armstrong |date=March 30 2009}} In the summer of 2005, Stephenson enrolled at [[Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School]], but he only attended the school for three days, before the school lost in the championship game of a youth league and he did not win the tournament MVP. The following week, Stephenson did not return to classes at Bishop Loughlin, and was attending [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn, New York)|Abraham Lincoln High School]] near his home in [[Coney Island]]. [[National Basketball Association]] players [[Stephon Marbury]] and [[Sebastian Telfair]] had also attended and played basketball at Lincoln High. Head coach Dwanye Morton said, "{Stephenson} always talked about outdoing Sebastian, outdoing Stephon,", and called him "The best I've ever had at Lincoln." Stephenson went on to lead the Railsplitters to the city title that year. Lincoln High repeated as champions his sophomore and junior years, while Stephenson won back-to-back Player of the Year honors from the ''[[New York Daily News]]''. In July 2008, Stephenson tried out for the [[USA men's national basketball team|United States national team]]'s under-18 team, but was cut because of chemistry reasons. On February 15, 2009, Stephenson passed fellow Lincoln High School alumnus Telfair's previous record of 2,785 points in the Brooklyn borough title game to become the all-time leading scorer for high school basketball in [[New York State]].{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/high_school/2009/02/15/2009-02-15_lance_stephenson_sets_scoring_record_as_.html |title=Lance Stephenson sets scoring record as Lincoln wins Brooklyn title |first=Mitch |last=Abramson |date=February 15 2009 |publisher=[[New York Daily News]]}} In March 2009, Stephenson led Lincoln High to an unprecedented fourth consecutive [[Public Schools Athletic League]] (PSAL) class AA championship. Stephenson scored a game-high 24 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to in the 78-56 final win against [[John F. Kennedy High School (Bronx, New York)|John F. Kennedy]], and helped Lincoln become the first school in city history to win four straight titles.{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/high_school/2009/03/21/2009-03-21_lance_stephenson_leads_lincoln_to_unprec.html |title=Lance Stephenson leads Lincoln to unprecedented fourth-straight crown |date=March 21 2009 |first=Ian |last=Begley |publisher=[[New York Daily News]]}} Stephenson's high school career ended in the New York State semifinal, where [[Rice High School (New York)|Rice High School]] beat Lincoln 77-50, and Stephenson was held to 12 points by Rice's [[Durand Scott]], who also beat out Stephenson for the ''Daily News''' New York City player of the year honor.{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/high_school/2009/05/11/2009-05-11_the_best_of_the_big_apple.html?page=0 |title=SThe best of the Big Apple: News hands out more high school honors |source=''[[New York Daily News]]'' |date=May 12 2009}} He ended his career with 2,946 points. In April 2009, Stephenson played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]], finishing with 12 points, six assists and three steals.{{cite news |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4035376 |title=Favors stars in high-flying game |first=Chirs |last=Lawlor |date=April 2 2009 |publisher=ESPN.com |work=RISE}} ==Off the court== As a sophomore, he was the youngest player featured in the movie ''[[Gunnin' for That No. 1 Spot]]'', which followed eight high school basketball prospects.[http://www.gunninmovie.com/players/lance_stephenson.php gunninmovie.com] In 2008 as a high school junior he was named to the annual ''[[USA Today]]'''s All-USA boys basketball team, the only non-senior to given that honor.[http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2008-all-usa-boys.htm USA Today's All-USA team] Stephenson received his "Born Ready" nickname from [[Bobbito Garcia]], a courtside announcer at [[Rucker Park]], in the summer of 2006 during a game against older players. Stephenson had just played in a youth all-star game as the only rising sophomore out of the 24 top high school players in the nation, and the adult game that followed was a player short. Garcia said, "I'd seen him go up against seasoned NBA veterans, seasoned college cats, high school kids two or three years older than him, and he was always reppin', so I just called it. He's Born Ready." Stephenson tattooed the nickname on his right biceps, and also allowed a video crew to document his life for an online [[reality show]] titled "Born Ready".{{cite news |url=http://www.tnr.com/story.html?id=89c1f6fc-f89a-4113-b5d2-b640359ac889 |title=Empty Garden: Why did New York stop growing basketball stars? |first=Jason |last=Zengerle |date=April 15 2009 |publisher=''[[The New Republic]]'' }} In January 2008, Stephenson was suspended from school for five days and missed two games following an altercation with a teammate.{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/high_school/2008/01/10/2008-01-10_lincoln_basketball_star_in_altercation.html |title=Lincoln Basketball Star in Altercation |date=January 10 2008 |publisher=''[[New York Daily News]]'' |first=Kristie |last=Ackert}} In October that year, he was arrested for groping a 17-year-old inside the school.{{cite news |title=Lincoln High School hoops phenom Lance Stephenson charged with school grope |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/ny_local/brooklyn/2008/10/18/2008-10-18_lincoln_high_school_hoops_phenom_lance_s.html#ixzz0FR54s3s6&B |date=October 18 2008 |first=Dorian |last=Block |publisher=''[[New York Daily News]]''}} He faced a Class B misdemeanor sexual assault charge, and his parents ended the "Born Ready" reality show following the arrest. ==Recruiting== As of May 20, 2009, the last day of NCAA's late signing period for basketball players, Stephenson had not declared or signed a [[letter of intent]] with the college he would attend that fall. In early 2009, Stephenson chose [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[St. John's Red Storm|St. John's]] and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] as his finalists{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/high_school/2009/03/26/2009-03-26_sources_lincoln_star_lance_stephenson_le.html |title=Sources: Lincoln star Lance Stephenson leaning toward Kansas over St. John's |source=''[[New York Daily News]]'' |first=Ian |last=Begley |author2=Mark Lelinwalla |date=March 26 2009}}, but he canceled two announcements, and his father said that he had narrowed his choice to Maryland and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/recruiting/basketball/2009-05-19-wall-kentucky_N.htm |title=All-USA point guard John Wall signs with Kentucky |date=May 20 2009 |publisher=''[[USA Today]]'' |first=Jim |last=Halley |author2=Jeff Zillgit}} His official visit to Maryland in February came under scrutiny after he was given a tour of the [[Under Armour]] headquarters during his visit. This may have constituted a recruiting violation, as Under Armour CEO [[Kevin Plank]] is a [[University of Maryland at College Park|Maryland]] graduate and on the university's board of trustees, and by NCAA rules, "representative of the institution's athletics interests" or a [[Booster club|booster]].{{cite news |url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2009/02/28/AR2009022802064.html |title=Shoe Company's Ties With Maryland, Link to Top Recruit Raise Questions |source=''[[Washington Post]]'' |first=Eric |last=Prisbell |author2=Steve Yanda |date=March 1 2009 |page=D01}} Stephenson initially told reporters he would announce which college he would be attending following the [[PSAL]] title game in March, but delayed the announcement until the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] on April 1, saying, "I already know where I'm going. This is not the right place [to make an announcement]."{{cite news |url=http://www.nypost.com/seven/03192009/sports/college/lincoln_star_quiet_160268.htm |title=LINCOLN STAR QUIET |first=Dan |last=Martin |publisher=''[[New York Post]]'' |date=March 19 2009}} On March 31, Stephenson, who had been expected to commit to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] during the All-American game's media event, instead announced that he would delay the announcement again. In April 2009, another top recruit [[Xavier Henry]], who had been released from his commitment to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] after coach [[John Calipari]] left to take the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] job, announced he would play for Kansas. Because Henry's commitment put Kansas at the 13-scholarship limit under [[NCAA]] rules, it ruled out a scholarship offer for Stephenson.{{cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/terrapins-insider/2009/04/henry_chooses_kansas_stephenso.html |title=Henry Chooses Kansas; Stephenson Still Deciding |first=Steve |last=Yanda |date=April 23 2009 |publisher=''[[The Washington Post]]'' |work=Terrapin Insider}} On May 20, the last day of the late signing period, Stephenson had not signed a letter of intent, but his father Lance Sr. told ''[[USA Today]]'' that he would not make a decision until his sexual assault case from October was resolved. The day before, a judge had [[Adjournment|adjourned]] his case until June 29. On June 30, [[Andy Katz]] of [[ESPN.com]] reported that Stephenson signed a financial aid agreement with the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|University of Cincinnati]] and, he joined them for the Bearcats for the 2009-10 season.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4298304 |title=Hoopster Stephenson headed to Cincy |first=Andy |last=Katz |authorlink=Andy Katz |date=June 30 2009 |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |work=Rise}} Questions remained over his eligibility because of his involvement in his documentary, but on November 6, 2009, the [[NCAA]] cleared him to play in Cincinnati's season opener against [[Prairie View A&M University]] on November 15 without missing any games.{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigeast/2009-11-06-cincinnati-stephenson_N.htm |title=NCAA clears Lance Stephenson to play at Cincinnati |date=November 6, 2009 |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} ==Professional Basketball== On April 7, 2010, Stephenson announced that he would forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2010/04/07/2010-04-07_former_lincoln_star_to_declare_for_nba_draft.html|title=Former Lincoln star Lance Stephenson to declare for NBA draft after one season at Cincinnati |date=April 7, 2010 |publisher=nydailynews.com}} ==References== {{reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://www.gobearcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/stephenson_lance00.html Cincinnati Bio] *{{imdb name|2958147|Lance Stephenson}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Stephenson, Lance}} [[Category:Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn, New York) alumni]] [[Category:African American basketball players]] [[Category:People from Brooklyn]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]]
